clue.text: Friend with space for magazine?

parts.note: put a space in the middle of Friend and it reads Fri end: the close of Friday; that phrase is also a magazine title

explanation.surface: Someone asking for a pal to be given a page or column in a periodical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Space' looks like column inches in print, but it means a gap typed inside the word Friend. WHEN SATURDAY COMES is a long-running British football fanzine.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: Fri end describes the moment the weekend's first day arrives, and that is also the name of a football magazine.

clue.text: See 28
Heartless man, the type to upset Lolita

indicators.note: upset tells us to knock the letters over and rearrange them
a heartless word has its middle cut out, so only the outside letters of man remain

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted man of the sort who would distress the girl in Nabokov's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' leaves MN from man; 'upset' rearranges MN with THE and TYPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lolita, the title girl of Nabokov's novel, is the archetypal sexually precocious young girl, a meaning the word took from that book.

clue.text: See 1
'Really unfortunate' — team star describing a poor performance

indicators.note: describing in its old sense of drawing a line around, so the anagram encloses the a
unfortunate says the letters of team star have come out badly and must be reordered

parts.note: a poor performance is an off act, a turn that is below par

explanation.surface: A grumble that a star player in the side has turned in a dismal display, which is really unfortunate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunate' rearranges TEAM STAR to ASMATTER; 'describing' puts A inside it after AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Really used as an emphatic adverb, as in 'really, I did', is the same as the phrase meaning in actual truth.

clue.text: Howl — American singer flipped over note

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits above the next
flipped means the letters for American singer are turned to run the other way

parts.note: Lulu is a Scottish pop singer, famous for Shout
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A US vocalist doing a somersault over a musical note and letting out a howl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipped' turns ALULU into ULULA, then 'over' puts it above TE. The singer is Lulu, and American only supplies A.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are verbs for letting out a long, wavering, wailing cry like a wolf or mourner.

clue.text: German's not one to put off

indicators.note: not one tells us to leave out the letter standing for one

parts.note: Dieter is a typical German man's name
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A remark that Germans are not the sort to be discouraged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German' is a person called Dieter, not the language.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to discourage someone from acting is to put them off doing it.

clue.text: Any trouble, hunt for uppity Northerners

indicators.note: trouble works as a verb here, stirring up the letters of any
uppity in a down clue reads as going upwards, so the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: to hunt for something is to seek it

explanation.surface: Any bother, and the search is on for some arrogant people from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' reorders ANY to YAN; 'uppity' turns SEEK into KEES.
explanation.definitionFit: In the American Civil War the Yankees were the people of the Union states, the Northerners.

clue.text: She lives with murder victim

parts.note: lives in the sense of exists, as in she is
Abel, killed by his brother Cain in Genesis, was the first murder victim

explanation.surface: A woman who shares her home with someone who was murdered.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabel is a female name, so it stands for a woman referred to as she.

clue.text: See 1
Touching? One still can have a little grope

parts.note: a means one, as in a single thing
but and still both mean nevertheless
a can is a tin

indicators.note: a little of the word grope is just its first letter

explanation.surface: A cheeky question: one person can still sneak in a quick grope?
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: things that are touching meet at a shared edge or border.

clue.text: A bad habit I'm keeping quiet — no time for animals

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so the jumble wraps around quiet
bad signals that the letters are in a poor, jumbled state
no time means the letter for time is dropped

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone owning up to a bad habit they keep secret, with no time to spare for pets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes T from HABITIM; 'bad' rearranges the rest to MHIBIA, and 'keeping' puts P in it after M.
explanation.definitionFit: Amphibia is the zoological class of frogs, newts and salamanders, so it is a group of creatures.

clue.text: Yes, it's a sin

parts.note: greed, or avarice, is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: Confirming that something is indeed sinful.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'agreed!' is a way of giving assent, the same as answering with a plain affirmative.

clue.text: Implant isn't working — not finished unfortunately

indicators.note: working means in operation, so the letters are put to work in a new order
not finished means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: ill means badly or unfortunately, as in ill-fated

explanation.surface: A medical implant has failed and the procedure, sadly, is incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges ISNT to INST; 'not finished' trims ILL to IL.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to instil an idea or habit is to implant it gradually in someone's mind.

clue.text: Not those snaring men, I suppose

indicators.note: snaring means trapping, so the outer word holds the others captive

parts.note: the opposite of those is these
OR, other ranks, stands for ordinary soldiers or men

explanation.surface: Someone guessing it was not those particular men who were caught in a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not those' gives the opposite word, these; 'men' is OR, other ranks, the army's term for ordinary soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to theorise is to form a hypothesis, to speculate or conjecture.

clue.text: Deciding what you're doing about leads

indicators.note: leads means goes in front, so the word for about comes first

parts.note: re means about or concerning
the solver reading this clue is, at that moment, solving a crossword

explanation.surface: Settling what you plan to do with some clues or tip-offs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads' looks like clues to follow up, but it says RE goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: resolving a question means deciding or settling it.

clue.text: Noisy lover is briefly on top, then on back

indicators.note: briefly means in short form, so is shrinks to the contracted 's

parts.note: the cream is the top, the very best part

indicators.note: back says this little word for regarding is turned round

parts.note: re means on, in the sense of concerning

explanation.surface: A racy picture of a loud partner going on top and then on their back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts IS to S; 'back' turns RE into ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Playful description: someone who cries out loudly is a screamer, here pictured in a passionate setting.

clue.text: Wander up country without getting burnt

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the country goes around the other piece

parts.note: Chad is a country in central Africa

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to err originally meant to stray or wander

explanation.surface: Travelling around a nation without getting sunburnt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like it means lacking, but here it has its old sense of outside, so the country goes around the reversed wander.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something charred has been scorched or blackened by fire.

clue.text: Letter will upset learned Muslims

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, reading upwards

parts.note: shall and will both form the future tense

explanation.surface: A written message that will distress some Islamic scholars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SHALL into LLAHS.
explanation.definitionFit: Mullahs are Muslim clerics trained in Islamic theology and law, so they are religious scholars.

clue.text: General loss of libido initially in group

indicators.note: loss of says a letter is taken away

parts.note: a cluster is a group of things together

indicators.note: initially means the start of the word libido is used

explanation.surface: A general fading of desire across a group of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' is the definition, not an adjective: George Custer, the US cavalry general killed at Little Bighorn.
explanation.definitionFit: George Armstrong Custer was a US Army cavalry general, best known for his last stand at Little Bighorn.

clue.text: I'm dismayed Papa is shouting out

indicators.note: is here places the letter for Papa in the middle of the word for shouting out

parts.note: to shout out is to cry out, so shouting out gives cries
Papa is P in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A child alarmed that their father is yelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Cripes is an old-fashioned exclamation of surprise or alarm, a way of saying one is taken aback.

clue.text: Playing most of time in school team

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the school

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school
v, short for versus, is how fixtures are written, as in Arsenal v Spurs, so playing gives v

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Playing for most of the time in a school side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' gives V because fixtures are written as one side v another. The team is a Liverpool football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Everton is a Premier League football club from Liverpool, so it is a side.

clue.text: Drawing up as telephone rings

indicators.note: rings means surrounds, so the words up as telephone encircle the answer

explanation.surface: Pulling up as the phone starts to ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rings' looks like the telephone's sound; it says the letters sit inside 'up as telephone'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastel is a picture made with soft chalky crayons, so it is a kind of artwork on paper.

clue.text: Hit town on hunch

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the second piece sits beneath the first

parts.note: T is an abbreviation for town, as on maps
a hunch is a hump, as on the back

explanation.surface: A local strike carried out on a mere gut feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to thump someone is to strike them hard.

clue.text: Girls run in underwear

indicators.note: in means the run goes inside the girls

parts.note: fillies is an old-fashioned slang word for girls
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Young women dashing about in their underclothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Frillies is informal for frilly women's lingerie, so it is a type of undergarment.

clue.text: Fuss picking up drink — it's a joke!

indicators.note: picking up as a radio picks up a signal, so the word is taken by ear

parts.note: a brew is a drink, especially tea or beer
ha ha is the laugh that greets a joke

explanation.surface: Someone causing a stir by grabbing a glass, then laughing it off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picking up' means hearing: BREW said aloud gives BROU.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a brouhaha is a noisy fuss or commotion.

clue.text: Writer's online work reviewed

parts.note: e stands for electronic, as in e-mail, so it means online

indicators.note: reviewed is read as re-viewed, looked at backwards

parts.note: toil is hard work

explanation.surface: An author's web-published piece getting critiqued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewed' looks like a critic's job; here it turns TOIL into LIOT.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot and T S Eliot are both famous authors in English.

clue.text: Top sides changed places

indicators.note: changed means the letters of top sides are swapped about

explanation.surface: Teams at the head of the league have swapped their league positions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'places' looks like league positions, but it is a verb: puts down.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to deposit something is to put it down somewhere.

clue.text: Cast make change with new actor

indicators.note: cast as in casting metal anew, so the letters are melted and reshaped

explanation.surface: A film cast reshuffled to bring in a new performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like a film's actors but rearranges MAKE CHANGE. Gene Hackman starred in The French Connection.
explanation.definitionFit: Gene Hackman was an Oscar-winning American film actor, star of The French Connection and Unforgiven.
